thread_title: S. flava var. maxima large form, N. Carolina (MKF91)
breadcrumb: S. flava var. maxima large form, N. Carolina (MKF91)

posts.body_html:
S. flava var. maxima is a variant that is devoid of red pigmentation in the body of the trap, especially in the throat. They are typically uncommon in populations, but show up here and there. These are not anthocyanin free plants; they sometimes do produce red pigments when damaged or under other environmental conditions.

Most of the maximas come from S. flava var. flava populations in the Carolinas, but occasionally, you'll find some maximas from Georgia and Florida. In those areas, the maximas are coming from mutated S. flava var. rugelii plants (the ones with the red throat).



Here's a S. flava var. maxima 'Large form' from North Carolina (MKF91), photos taken 5/10/13:






These plants can turn solid yellow under optimal conditions, which makes a S. flava var. maxima so desirable:


The lid on this thing is turning rather yellow, but it can become even more pronounced:

posts.body_html:
New photos, taken 4/6/15. It's taken a very long time to get this plant to produce large pitchers, but the tag don't like, these traps are pretty big! Of course, hard to tell from the photos, but that's cuz I don't always carry a ruler around with me:



This is a really beautiful plant despite the out of focus picture. The rhizome is about "normal" sized so it'll be interesting to see how gigantic the trap gets in the next year or two:
